headline: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani calls Netanyahu a 'war criminal'
summary: The New York City official says the Israeli PM should be sent to The Hague after facing ICC charges.
details: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has described Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as a 'war criminal' and stated that his place is in The Hague, Netherlands.
The comments come as Netanyahu is expected to visit New York City in September for the UN General Assembly.
Mamdani told a US media outlet that he is currently in active discussions with the New York City Law Department regarding the legal authority of the NYPD to arrest a foreign leader.
The New York City Police Department (NYPD) falls under the mayoral oversight, and Mamdani is exploring whether the police force can legally execute an arrest warrant.
This follows the International Criminal Court (ICC) issuing arrest warrants for Benjamin Netanyahu and former Israeli Defense Minister Yoav Gallant over the conflict in Gaza.
Israel has officially rejected these ICC allegations and charges.
caption:
Can the NYPD arrest a foreign leader? NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani says Netanyahu is a 'war criminal' who belongs in The Hague.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has described Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as a 'war criminal' and stated that his place is in The Hague, Netherlands.

The comments come as Netanyahu is expected to visit New York City in September for the UN General Assembly.

Mamdani told a US media outlet that he is currently in active discussions with the New York City Law Department regarding the legal authority of the NYPD to arrest a foreign leader.

The New York City Police Department (NYPD) falls under the mayoral oversight, and Mamdani is exploring whether the police force can legally execute an arrest warrant.

This follows the International Criminal Court (ICC) issuing arrest warrants for Benjamin Netanyahu and former Israeli Defense Minister Yoav Gallant over the conflict in Gaza.

Israel has officially rejected these ICC allegations and charges.

headline_marked: Govt to launch [[‘Probashi Card’ for expatriates in August]]
headline: Govt to launch ‘Probashi Card’ for expatriates in August
summary: The pilot project will offer 10 special benefits, including airport lounge access and healthcare discounts, to empower Bangladeshis living abroad.
details: The Bangladesh government will launch a pilot project for the 'Probashi Card' in August. The initiative was decided during a meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
The card aims to enhance the social status, empowerment, and financial incentives for expatriates. It will feature a 'dual currency' system to facilitate international payments and banking services.

Key benefits include complimentary airport lounge access, fast-track immigration services, and 'meet and greet' services at international airports. Cardholders will also receive discounts on flight tickets and hotel bookings.

Other perks include discounted healthcare at private hospitals, priority in land registration and utility services, and free repatriation of remains in case of death. It also offers priority in NID, passport, and consular services.
The pilot phase will begin in mid-August with Janata Bank issuing the first set of debit cards. The government aims to distribute 50,000 cards by December and 200,000 by June next year.
In the second phase, the Probashi Kalyan Bank will handle all card operations. The Prime Minister has also directed officials to ensure that Bangladeshis worldwide are covered under this scheme.
caption:
Airport lounges, fast-track immigration, and healthcare discounts—the new 'Probashi Card' is coming this August!

The Bangladesh government will launch a pilot project for the 'Probashi Card' in August. The initiative was decided during a meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.

The card aims to enhance the social status, empowerment, and financial incentives for expatriates. It will feature a 'dual currency' system to facilitate international payments and banking services.

Key benefits include complimentary airport lounge access, fast-track immigration services, and 'meet and greet' services at international airports. Cardholders will also receive discounts on flight tickets and hotel bookings.

Other perks include discounted healthcare at private hospitals, priority in land registration and utility services, and free repatriation of remains in case of death. It also offers priority in NID, passport, and consular services.

The pilot phase will begin in mid-August with Janata Bank issuing the first set of debit cards. The government aims to distribute 50,000 cards by December and 200,000 by June next year.

In the second phase, the Probashi Kalyan Bank will handle all card operations. The Prime Minister has also directed officials to ensure that Bangladeshis worldwide are covered under this scheme.
